key_insight: SAGEAgent treats multimodal survival prediction as a sequential decision problem, learning when to stop acquiring more diagnostic modalities to balance accuracy and clinical burden.
clinical_relevance: This could help support more efficient oncology workflows by avoiding unnecessary tests while still preserving useful survival prediction performance.
method: LLM-based agent makes stepwise modality-acquisition decisions in ordered clinical workflows
Uses clinical tools to convert numeric predictions into text for reasoning
Adds episodic memory for similar cases and semantic memory for reusable decision patterns
evidence_signal: On a glioma cohort spanning TCGA-LGG, TCGA-GBM, and BraTS with four modalities, the method achieved competitive survival prediction while reducing average acquisition burden by 55%.
watch_item: The approach should be validated carefully before use in real care because decisions depend on ordered modality availability, memory retrieval quality, and the risks of missing information.
paper_title: SAGEAgent: A Self-Evolving Agent for Cost-Aware Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Survival Prediction
